notes: Tests whether the arm carries the reference's framing (temperature as the master variable) rather than reciting a dictionary definition.

turns.content: Why does the reference call temperature the master variable?

must_contain: states temperature sets DO capacity — warmer water holds less oxygen
states it accelerates biological and chemical rates
states it shifts EC readings (raw EC rises ~2% per °C)
states the other five parameters should be interpreted relative to temperature
must_not: treats temperature as just one parameter among six with no coupling
invents a coupling not in the context

turns.content: Our temperature rose 3 °C this week and DO fell. Event or expected?

must_contain: states a temperature rise should always be paired with an expected DO decline, so the pairing alone is not an event
points to the thermal-discharge signature (temperature up strongly, DO down proportionally, other chemistry flat) as the thing to rule in or out
recommends checking EC, pH, ORP and turbidity to separate natural warming from a thermal discharge
must_not: declares a pollution event from temperature and DO alone
